evals.name: composition-avoids-ijpl-apis
evals.prompt: I am building a Jewel composable for an IntelliJ plugin. Is it okay for the composable to call Registry.get() and ProjectManager.getInstance() during composition if I wrap it in SwingBridgeTheme?
evals.expected_output: Guidance that Jewel/Compose composition should not directly or indirectly access IntelliJ Platform APIs; platform work belongs in a presenter/controller boundary or a tiny injected fakeable collaborator when unavoidable.
expectations: Says not to access IntelliJ Platform APIs directly or indirectly inside composition.
Allows an injected fakeable collaborator only when access is unavoidable.
Mentions threading or Compose stability implications of platform APIs.
Does not imply SwingBridgeTheme makes platform API access in composition safe.

evals.name: jewel-intellij-icon-key-loading
evals.prompt: I need to render a custom SVG icon in a Jewel-based IntelliJ plugin UI. The icon has an Old UI resource at icons/actions/run.svg and a New UI resource at icons/expui/actions/run.svg. Should I just call Compose painterResource, or is there a Jewel way to define and render this?
evals.expected_output: Guidance to define an IntelliJIconKey with old and new UI paths and a classloader context, then render it with Jewel Icon(key = ...) or Image(iconKey = ...), avoiding raw painterResource so Jewel/IntelliJ icon patching and UI variants work correctly.
expectations: Uses IntelliJIconKey for the old and new UI resource paths rather than a single raw painterResource call.
Includes both icons/actions/run.svg and icons/expui/actions/run.svg in the icon key definition.
Uses an explicit class context such as MyIcons::class.java for classloader resource lookup.
Renders with Jewel Icon(key = ..., contentDescription = ...) or Image(iconKey = ...).
Explains that raw painterResource bypasses Jewel or IntelliJ icon-key handling for UI variants, theme patching, or classpath portability.
